title: [test] pip install radintake 0.2.0 from PyPI in clean venvs on Windows and Linux runs the quickstart
description:
Lane relpub (rad-s2g.14), task 2 of 2. It follows rad-s2g.14.2 by streakOrder. Model standard: an end-to-end install check on two operating systems.

What to test: the published package, not the working tree.
- Windows (this host): make a fresh venv OUTSIDE the repo (a temp dir), then pip install radintake==0.2.0 from PyPI with the default index only. Run the README quickstart against a synthetic fixture (for example a page from tests/fixtures or one generated on the fly; never IU data). Check that a typed result comes back with the expected header fields and that nothing is written to disk by default.
- Linux: do the same inside a clean python:3.11 container (docker run --rm with the fixture mounted read-only), installing tesseract-ocr via apt in the container if the quickstart needs OCR.
- Check the PyPI project page metadata through the JSON API: the version is 0.2.0, the long description is markdown, and it has no relative links.
- Check that the README PyPI badge points at pypi/v/radintake.

Optionally add a script, scripts/verify_pypi_release.py (takes a version and a fixture path, builds a venv, installs, runs the quickstart and prints a JSON summary), so the check can be repeated. If you add it, it must not run in the default pytest collection.

IF rad-s2g.14.2 closed on the blocked-on-publisher branch (nothing on PyPI): do not fake a pass. Instead, show the same quickstart passing from the locally built 0.2.0 wheel in clean venvs on both operating systems, and record in the close note that the install-from-PyPI check is still pending the owner's publisher registration. The feature rad-s2g.14 then stays open.
acceptance_criteria: Published case (rad-s2g.14.2 closed on branch A): in a fresh Windows venv outside the repo and in a fresh python:3.11 Linux container, pip install radintake==0.2.0 resolves from pypi.org (pip output pasted), import radintake reports __version__ 0.2.0, and the README quickstart on a synthetic fixture exits 0 with a typed result containing header fields; the PyPI JSON for 0.2.0 shows description_content_type text/markdown and a description with no relative links; the GitHub release v0.2.0 exists. Not-yet-published case (rad-s2g.14.2 closed on branch B awaiting owner approval, or branch C blocked on publisher): the same quickstart passes from the locally built 0.2.0 wheel in a fresh Windows venv and a fresh python:3.11 Linux container, and the close note says the PyPI install check is still pending and why (owner approval or publisher registration), citing the run URL or error from 14.2; the feature rad-s2g.14 stays open. In every case no IU data or anything under data/ is used, no file is left outside the temp dirs, and the doer does not wait on the release workflow.
notes: PLAN-REVIEW FIX (2026-11-26), supersedes the last paragraph of the description: the local-wheel fallback applies when rad-s2g.14.2 closed on branch B (awaiting owner approval) as well as on branch C (blocked on publisher). See the acceptance field.

title: [impl] Tag v0.2.0 and publish through release.yml to TestPyPI then PyPI with GitHub release
description:
Lane relpub (rad-s2g.14), task 1 of 2. It starts only after lane relprep (rad-s2g.14.1) has been reviewed, because publishing cannot be undone. Model standard: an operational, step-by-step release with a defined stop condition.

The owner approved publishing radintake 0.2.0 on 2026-11-26 (see rad-s2g.14).

Do:
1. On an up-to-date main containing rad-s2g.14.1, create the annotated tag v0.2.0 and push it, which triggers .github/workflows/release.yml (from rad-s2g.11.2). The tag must point at the commit whose pyproject version is 0.2.0.
2. The workflow publishes to TestPyPI and then to PyPI through trusted publishing, behind the testpypi and pypi GitHub environments. If an environment needs manual approval, only the owner can give it: report that it is waiting and do not try to bypass it.
3. STOP CONDITION: if publishing fails with an OIDC or trusted-publisher error (no publisher registered on TestPyPI or PyPI), stop. Report to the owner that a pending publisher must be added on each index (repo varmakvl/radintake, workflow release.yml, environments testpypi and pypi). Leave the tag and workflow in place and close this task with that report. Never use, create or ask for API tokens, and never upload by hand with twine.
4. Before publishing to PyPI, check the TestPyPI upload locally: in a fresh venv, pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ radintake==0.2.0, then import it and check that __version__ is 0.2.0.
5. Once PyPI has 0.2.0, create the GitHub release v0.2.0 (gh release create) using the CHANGELOG 0.2.0 section as the notes, unless the workflow already created it.

Judge results by what you can observe yourself (PyPI and TestPyPI JSON APIs, pip install, gh release view), not by whether a CI run shows green.

Expected files: none or minimal (fix release.yml only if it has a real defect; such a fix needs a new patch version, never a re-upload of 0.2.0).
acceptance_criteria: Close on exactly one of three branches. (A) PUBLISHED: https://pypi.org/pypi/radintake/0.2.0/json and https://test.pypi.org/pypi/radintake/0.2.0/json both return HTTP 200 and list a wheel and an sdist; gh release view v0.2.0 shows a release whose notes match the CHANGELOG 0.2.0 section; tag v0.2.0 on origin points at the commit whose version is 0.2.0. (B) AWAITING OWNER APPROVAL: tag v0.2.0 is pushed to origin and points at the 0.2.0 commit; the release.yml run is waiting on a GitHub environment approval; the close note records the run URL (gh run list --workflow release.yml), which environments are waiting (testpypi and/or pypi), and the exact owner action (approve the pending deployment for that environment in the run page, then approve pypi after testpypi); whatever is already published is listed. (C) BLOCKED ON PUBLISHER: tag v0.2.0 is pushed, release.yml is unchanged or minimally fixed, and the close note quotes the OIDC or trusted-publisher error and lists the exact pending-publisher settings the owner must add (repo varmakvl/radintake, workflow release.yml, environments testpypi and pypi). On every branch: no API token was used or requested, nothing was uploaded by hand, and the doer did not wait on a CI run it cannot move forward -- one status check after the tag push decides the branch.
notes: PLAN-REVIEW FIX (2026-11-26), supersedes steps 2 and 4 of the description where they conflict: release.yml (from rad-s2g.11.2) is gated by approval environments, so the normal state after the tag push is a run waiting for the owner. Do not wait on it. After pushing the tag, check the run once with gh run list / gh run view and close on the matching acceptance branch: A published, B awaiting owner approval (record the run URL, the waiting environments and the owner action), or C blocked on publisher. Step 4 (check the TestPyPI install before PyPI) only applies if the owner approves the testpypi environment separately before pypi and TestPyPI already has 0.2.0 when you check; otherwise skip it and note that it was skipped. Step 5 (GitHub release) only applies on branch A.
